strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing headless.run.drive can derive bounded product evidence from current allowlisted artifacts and completion ledger facts before product stop/continue decisions.
Product completion gates move closer to runtime-owned evidence instead of caller-owned category assertions.
Rust validates the derivation authorization, artifact allowlist, hashes, symlink/file-kind checks, and completion-boundary binding.
Headless replay uses bounded fingerprints and category counts instead of raw Product Charter, manifest, spec, or ledger text.
Drive results can surface bounded next action to record a product decision using runtime-derived evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing headless.run.drive can explicitly derive a bounded product evidence matrix from allowlisted current artifacts, persist it once, replay it, and let product_completion_decision consume its fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M51.3/M51.3.1 made product decisions durable and unique but still trusted caller-assembled product evidence categories.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless caller could still provide self-consistent but stale or incomplete product evidence metadata as the basis for stop/continue decisions.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M51.2 accepted-completion routing, M51.3 product decision recording, and M51.3.1 same-boundary uniqueness enforcement because this changes the product evidence authority source.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends existing headless.run.drive rather than adding a JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The matrix is bounded runtime evidence used by the decision path, not a report/history/readiness/verdict/inspection/dashboard wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust validates explicit derivation authorization, fixed artifact allowlist, expected SHA-256 hashes, regular UTF-8 non-symlink file kind, current phase manifest gate content, and completion-boundary binding before ledger append or product decision consumption.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can rely on a runtime-derived matrix fingerprint instead of interpreting raw artifacts or fabricating category lists externally.
answers.milestone_progress: This is the first M52 slice replacing caller-owned product truth with Rust-owned product evidence derivation.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M52.1 updates manifests and runtime/protocol code for bounded product evidence matrix derivation. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and this is not a report-only surface.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive can derive a bounded product evidence matrix from a fixed artifact allowlist with expected SHA-256 hashes
derived matrix evidence is bound to accepted-completion, terminal-completion, and completion-closure fingerprints
product_completion_decision can consume the derived matrix fingerprint instead of caller-owned category truth
stale artifact hashes or unsafe artifacts fail closed before matrix or product-decision ledger mutation
replay is duplicate-free for matrix and product-decision evidence
no new JSON-RPC method and no report/readiness/history/verdict/inspection/dashboard wrapper is added

RPC and ledger metadata remain bounded and exclude raw prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, raw Product Charter or manifest text, diagnostics, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_derives_product_evidence_matrix_and_decides validates authorized matrix derivation, product-decision consumption, replay, bounded metadata, and duplicate-free events.
Rust negative test headless_run_drive_rejects_stale_product_evidence_artifact_hash validates stale artifact hash denial before matrix or product-decision mutation.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests validate product_evidence_derivation, product_evidence_matrix, and derived_product_evidence_matrix_fingerprint transport shape without VSIX-owned policy.

accepted_capability: Existing headless.run.drive derives and persists bounded runtime-owned product evidence matrix metadata for product completion decisions
safety_boundary: Expected SHA-256 required for every artifact
Existing regular UTF-8 non-symlink artifacts only
Completion boundary fingerprints must match before derivation and decision consumption
Ledger and RPC expose only bounded ids, counts, category names, artifact paths, hashes, next action, and SHA-256 fingerprints
VSIX validates transport shape only; Rust owns evidence policy
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No provider/tool/verifier execution, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No raw Product Charter, manifest, spec, ledger, prompt, provider, file, command, output, environment, absolute path, canonical path, or secret exposure
No milestone closeout in this implementation PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a product evidence inspection RPC was rejected because the runtime decision path needs evidence authority, not observability.
Keeping caller-supplied categories as source of truth was rejected because it leaves product completion outside Rust authority.
Parsing raw Product Charter text into RPC output was rejected because it would leak artifact content and create a summary surface.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred so this remains a bounded vertical slice.
technical_debt: The matrix initially derives from a fixed artifact allowlist and manifest gate structure; richer internal Product Charter modeling remains future M52 work.
crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only in a cohesive future refactor.
M50.1 journey admission atomicity remains separate non-blocking technical debt.
next_capability_rationale: If accepted, the next M52 phase should harden freshness or broaden runtime-owned evidence categories only if it changes product-decision authority rather than adding an inspection wrapper.
